AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

 5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Najarian congratulated his brother-in-law, Dr. Steven Yacoubian, an
  orthopedic surgeon and a Lt. Commander in the US Navy, for receiving a medal of
  recognition after partaking in operation “Keen Sword” this October at Camp Foster, a US
  Marine Base in Okinawa, Japan.

  Councilmember Brotman commended the Sustainability Office for a successful repair café
  and clothing swap event this past weekend. The repair café and clothing swap event is held
  every three months.

  Councilmember Gharpetian attended the Glendale Latino Association Annual Toy Drive
  Mixer at Porto’s Bakery. He congratulated the Armenian Society of Los Angeles’ 68th
  Anniversary. Gharpetian asked staff to provide an update on the digital sign ordinance. He
  reminded council that he wishes to recognize the month of December as Family Celebration
  and Appreciation Month and asked staff to organize small events to honor our families.
  Gharpetian requested to agendize a discussion regarding the appointment for a seat on the
  Burbank-Glendale-Pasadena Airport Authority Commission. He congratulated Kathryn
  Barger and Nathan Hochman for being re-elected/elected and stated that it is important to
  pay attention to what is happening statewide and nationwide since this will affect us one way
  or another. Gharpetian expressed his wish of having faith-based invocators for the two
  council meetings in December.

  Mayor Asatryan stated that she had a productive and fruitful meeting with Ascencia and that
  a report will be presented to council for discussion. She took a trip to South Korea and
  signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Incheon Free Economic Zone (IFEZA), to
  foster mutual economic growth through collaboration in the entertainment industry. Asatryan
  stated that IFEZA Commissioner Dr. Yoon Won-sok will visit the City of Glendale in January
  2025 to look at spaces to bring forth Korean entertainment and K-Pop events and asked
  staff to collaborate. Mayor Asatryan also requested to agendize for discussion a report on
  programs to assist small businesses and restaurants facing Steep commercial rent
  increases.
